subject: Request: development governance evidence (code review, CI, secrets, change management) for SOC2/SIG
messages:
From: Acuity Security - auditor <auditor@acuitysec.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30 09:12 AM UTC
Subject: Evidence request: development governance controls (SOC2/SIG)

Hi Soojin,

As part of the SOC2 + SIG review for GreenLine Financial, we need a small evidence package for your "development governance" controls. Specifically we are looking for:

- Code review process and a recent export showing PR review completion metrics (last 90 days)
- CI/CD controls: pipeline snapshots, test coverage gating, and an example pipeline run logs
- Secrets management: rotation schedule for production secrets, proof of KMS usage/encryption at rest
- Change management: list of change requests tied to production deployments for the last quarter and approvals

Could you please send items or a pointer to a shared folder by EOD Wednesday, Dec 2? If any items are sensitive, a secure link or redacted CSV is fine.

Thanks,
Mark L. (Acuity Security)
Auditor
 [attachment: auditor_checklist_2026Q4.pdf (PDF)]

From: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Acuity Security - auditor <auditor@acuitysec.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-30 10:03 AM UTC
Subject: Re: Evidence request: development governance controls (SOC2/SIG)

Mark — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Dev (Dev Patel) and Compliance (Lauren) to assemble the artifacts. High-level notes up front so you have context:

- Code review: we enforce mandatory reviewers for all PRs that touch prod services, plus an automated merge-block if required checks fail. We can export PR metadata (approvals, reviewer ids, timestamps).
- CI/CD: pipelines run in isolated runners with signed manifests; test gating is enforced for all non-doc PRs.
- Secrets: production secrets are in AWS KMS-backed Parameter Store; rotation events are logged to the audit stream.
- Change mgmt: we use CHG tickets in Jira for any infra or prod-release change; approvals are required from SRE and Security for changes to sensitive services.

Dev — can you attach the requested snapshots and a small readme describing each file? Lauren — any compliance mapping you want included?

Cheers,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Manager, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
[signature: soojin_lee_sig.png]

From: dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Acuity Security - auditor <auditor@acuitysec.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 15:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: development governance controls (SOC2/SIG)

Thanks — attaching the artifacts below and summarizing contents for the reviewer. Files uploaded to shared Drive link in the related_links field and attached stubs are included here.

Attachments (stubs included):
- pr_workflow_snapshot_20261129.pdf (PDF) — export of PRs from repo: redwood-inference-core for 2026-09-01 to 2026-11-29. Includes approval timestamps, reviewer ids, and whether automated checks passed.
- ci_pipeline_snapshot_20261129.tar.gz (archive) — YAML pipeline manifests and a sanitized pipeline run log (ci-run-2026-11-29.log) showing run IDs, test gating, and artifact signing steps.
- secrets_rotation_2026Q4.csv (CSV) — rotation events for KMS-backed secrets (redacted values), includes rotated_at, rotated_by, secret_id, rotation_policy_id.
- change_requests_export_202611.log (text) — exported CHG tickets referencing deployments; column includes CHG-id, service, change_type, approvers, deploy_date.

Summary highlights and control mapping:
- Code review enforcement: PR protection rules + OIDC-based pipeline checks. See PR export for >98% reviewer presence on prod-impact PRs in last 90 days.
- CI/CD controls: pipelines are executed on ephemeral runners, artifacts signed with internal keys, and manual gates exist for production deploy jobs requiring two approvers. Example log shows gate hold + approval sequence.
- Secrets: production secrets stored in AWS Parameter Store with KMS CMKs; rotation schedule is quarterly for high-privilege keys, and rotation events are ingested to our audit stream (see secrets CSV).
- Change mgmt: CHG tickets CHG-4821, CHG-4890 and CHG-4922 correspond to two platform releases and one emergency patch; approvals captured in the exported log.

If you need raw console access or additional traces, I can generate an RBAC-limited view and a time-bound link.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference
[attachment: ci-run-2026-11-29.log (text)]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Acuity Security - auditor <auditor@acuitysec.com>, soojin_lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-03 16:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Evidence request: development governance controls (SOC2/SIG)

Mark — thanks for reviewing the packages. A couple of clarifications that often come up from assessors:

- Secrets encryption: all KMS CMKs in prod are customer-managed (AWS KMS), and CMK key policies and rotation are documented in the GDrive folder. The secrets CSV shows key_id references rather than plaintext.
- Retention: PR metadata and CI logs are retained for 12 months; raw build artifacts for 90 days. The retention policy doc is in the shared folder and is linked above.
- Change approvals: for any change touching payment or data-storage services we require SRE + Security approval. The CHG export includes the approver usernames; we can provide an auditor-only view for live verification if needed.

If you want a short mapping table between SOC2 control IDs and the artifacts delivered, see the SOC2 mapping spreadsheet at the Drive link. Happy to set up a 30-min walkthrough next week if that helps.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Compliance Operations
Redwood Inference
[signature: lauren_bishop_sig.png]
